The [preview deck](preview.html) is built by this site.
This page is the source behind it.

## A tabset

```markdown
::: {.panel-tabset}

### First

The first tab.

### Second

The second, reached with the next arrow press.

:::
```

Each tab is a fragment, so the arrow keys step through them without leaving the keyboard.

## Opening on a given tab

```markdown
::: {.panel-tabset tab-active="2"}

### One

### Two

:::
```

The slide arrives with the second tab open.
The attribute is emitted as `data-tab-active` in the HTML.

## Fragments inside a tab

```markdown
::: {.panel-tabset}

### With reveals

- []{.fragment} First point.
- []{.fragment} Second point.

### Plain

:::
```

Fragments inside a tab are indexed within it, so the points arrive before the next tab does.

## Several tabsets on one slide

```markdown
::: {.panel-tabset}

### A

### B

:::

::: {.panel-tabset}

### X

### Y

:::
```

They are navigated one after another rather than in parallel.

## Printing

Each tab is placed on its own page in a PDF export, so a printed deck shows all of them.

Opt a slide out where that is not wanted:

```markdown
## A slide {tabset-skip-pdf-clone="true"}
```

Its tabsets then stay on one page, showing the active tab alone.

The repository ships a short, standalone starting point you can copy: [`example.qmd`](https://github.com/mcanouil/quarto-revealjs-tabset/blob/main/example.qmd).
